Yes, this is quite doable. Here's what I found:

**Current `enable` behavior** (setup.go:645-659): checks `paths.WorktreeRoot()` and exits with "Not a git repository" — clean place to hook in.

**`gh` CLI status**: not used anywhere in the codebase today. Adding it means shelling out via `exec.Command` (no Go dep on `github.com/cli/cli`).

**`gh` capabilities we need are all available**:
- Presence: `exec.LookPath("gh")`
- Auth check: `gh auth status` (installed ≠ authenticated)
- Default owner: `gh api user --jq .login` → authenticated user's login
- Orgs list: `gh api user/orgs --jq '.[].login'` — requires `read:org` scope (your token has it; if missing we'd fall back to user-only)
- Create + wire remote + push in one shot: `gh repo create <owner>/<name> --private --source=. --remote=origin --push`

**Recommended flow order** (because `--source=.` requires an existing local repo):
1. `git init` + initial `.gitignore`/branch setup
2. Stage files, show commit-message confirmation, create initial commit
3. `gh repo create owner/name --private --source=. --push` (one call creates remote, adds origin, pushes)
4. Then fall into the normal `runSetupFlow` path

**Things to decide before I build**:
- **Default visibility** — private vs. public (I'd default to private with a prompt)
- **If `gh` is missing or unauthenticated** — just print a hint (`brew install gh && gh auth login`) and fall through to the existing "not a git repo" error, or offer to `git init` locally without a remote?
- **Default owner in the suggestion** — user account, or pick from a `huh` select of `[user, ...orgs]`?
- **Folder-name sanitization** — GitHub names allow `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; we'd slugify (spaces → `-`, strip others)
- **Accessibility mode** — use `NewAccessibleForm` like the rest of the CLI (already a pattern here)

Want me to draft an implementation plan with file-level changes, or jump straight to coding once you've picked defaults for the four questions above?

Good — here's my proposal for params. I'll keep the kebab-case, same style as the existing `enable` flags:

**Flags (all optional; presence of all three lets you run non-interactively):**
- `--init-repo` *(bool)* — don't prompt; accept `git init` on a non-repo folder. Paired opposite `--no-init-repo` to decline without the prompt and exit like today.
- `--repo-name <name>` — GitHub repo name. Skips the suggest/confirm prompt. Pre-validates against GitHub's allowed charset and (if authenticated) availability.
- `--repo-owner <owner>` — user or org login. Skips the owner selector. Validated against `gh api user` + orgs list.
- `--repo-visibility <public|private|internal>` — skips the visibility prompt. (`internal` only allowed on orgs.)
- `--no-github` — do the local `git init` + initial commit, but don't touch GitHub. Useful if `gh` is missing/unauth or user just wants local.
- `--initial-commit-message <msg>` — skip the commit-message confirmation.

Everything stays interactive by default; flags only suppress their matching prompt.

**Name-availability check**: yes — `gh repo view <owner>/<name>` exits non-zero when not found, which is what we want. We'd run it after the user picks a name and either accept it or loop back to the prompt with a "already exists" hint. (Race condition on the final create is still possible; we just surface `gh repo create`'s error there.)

**Flow when `gh` is missing/unauthenticated** (per your answer):
1. Ask "No git repo here — `git init` now? [Y/n]"
2. If yes → init + confirm commit message + initial commit
3. Print "`gh` not found (or not logged in). Install with `brew install gh && gh auth login`, then `entire enable` again to add a GitHub remote. Skipping remote for now."
4. Fall into the existing `runSetupFlow`

**Implementation sketch** (all in one new file, no changes to existing strategy/session code):
- New file: `cmd/entire/cli/setup_github.go` — holds `runGitHubBootstrap(ctx, w, opts)` and its helpers (`ghAvailable`, `ghAuthenticated`, `ghDefaultOwner`, `ghListOwners`, `ghRepoExists`, `gitInitAndCommit`, plus the `huh` forms using `NewAccessibleForm`).

- New enable flags wired next to the existing ones around setup.go:722-733.
- Tests: `setup_github_test.go` with `gh` invocations faked via a `runner func(...) (string, error)` seam so tests don't shell out.

1. High: bootstrap commits can fail on fresh machines because the new repo is never configured with `user.name`/`user.email`, and the commit path does not disable GPG signing. That will fail for users without global git identity configured, and can also fail when `commit.gpgsign=true` but signing is unavailable. This repo already treats those as real hazards in test helpers by explicitly setting identity and `commit.gpgsign=false` for fresh repos ([testutil.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil/testutil.go:33)). As written, `entire enable --init-repo` is likely to break in exactly the “brand-new folder” scenario this feature is meant to support.

Medium: contradictory bootstrap flags are accepted and resolve in a surprising way. `enable` exposes both `--init-repo` and `--no-init-repo` ([setup.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:749)), but there is no validation for that combination. - New `ensureGitIdentity()` runs before every bootstrap commit: checks `git config --get user.{name,email}` at any scope; if missing, sources from `gh api user` (with `{id}+{login}@users.noreply.github.com` noreply fallback for private-email accounts); falls back to an interactive prompt or a clear non-interactive error pointing at `git config --global`.
```markdown
## Summary

Lets `entire enable` bootstrap a brand-new folder all the way to a working
repo — `git init`, initial commit, and a matching GitHub repository via
the `gh` CLI — instead of exiting with "Not a git repository".

## Motivation

Today, running `entire enable` in a non-git folder is a dead end. Users
have to `git init`, create a GitHub repo, wire up a remote, and then come
back. This PR folds that dance into the same command.

## Flow

1. Prompt: *"No git repository in `my-project`. Initialize one here?"*
2. `git init`
3. If `gh` is installed and authenticated:
   - Pick the owner (authenticated user + orgs from `gh api user/orgs`)
   - Suggest a repo name from the folder (slugified), check availability
     via `gh repo view`, let the user pick a different one if taken
   - Pick visibility (public / private / internal — `internal` only
     shown for orgs)
4. Confirm the initial commit message (default: `Initial commit`)
5. Stage + commit
6. `gh repo create <owner>/<name> --<visibility> --source=. --remote=origin --push`
7. Fall through to the normal `runSetupFlow` (agent selection, hooks, etc.)

If `gh` is missing or unauthenticated, the local `git init` + initial
commit still happens and we print a hint:

```
gh CLI not found. Install it from https://cli.github.com/ and run
`gh auth login` to add a GitHub remote. Continuing with local
initialization only.
```

All prompts use `NewAccessibleForm` so `ACCESSIBLE=1` works as expected.

## Flags

All optional; each suppresses its matching interactive prompt, so
automation can drive the flow end-to-end without a TTY.

- `--init-repo` / `--no-init-repo` — accept or decline the `git init`
  prompt. These two are mutually exclusive.
- `--repo-name` — GitHub repo name (validated against GitHub's charset).
- `--repo-owner` — GitHub user or org login.
- `--repo-visibility` — `public`, `private`, or `internal`.
- `--no-github` — local `git init` + initial commit only; skip GitHub.
- `--initial-commit-message` — override the default `Initial commit`.

## Fresh-machine safety (commit 2)

The initial commit has to work even when the user hasn't set up git yet:

- **Identity**: `ensureGitIdentity` checks `git config user.{name,email}`
  at any scope; if missing, it sources name + email from `gh api user`
  (falling back to `{id}+{login}@users.noreply.github.com` when the
  user's email is private), otherwise it prompts, otherwise it errors
  with a pointer to `git config --global`. Values are written to the
  local repo config only — global state is never mutated.
- **GPG**: the bootstrap commit runs with `-c commit.gpgsign=false` so a
  globally inherited `commit.gpgsign=true` with no working signer doesn't
  break the first commit. Subsequent commits still respect the user's
  global signing setting.

## Commits

- `Bootstrap git repo and GitHub remote from 'entire enable'` — the
  feature itself.
- `Make bootstrap commits work on fresh machines` — identity + gpgsign.
- `Reject --init-repo and --no-init-repo together` — one-line
  `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive` so automation surfaces the flag error
  instead of silently honoring `--no-init-repo`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `mise run check` passes (fmt + lint + unit + integration + Vogon
      canary + external-agent canary) — already green locally
- [ ] Manual: fresh empty folder → `entire enable` with no flags walks
      through all the prompts and pushes to GitHub
- [ ] Manual: fresh folder → `entire enable --init-repo --no-github
      --initial-commit-message "init"` completes non-interactively, no
      GitHub call
- [ ] Manual: on a machine with no `gh` → the hint prints and the local
      `git init` + commit still succeed
- [ ] Manual: `entire enable --init-repo --no-init-repo` surfaces
      cobra's "mutually exclusive" error
- [ ] Manual: existing git repo → `entire enable` behaves exactly as
      before (bootstrap path is skipped)

## Notes for reviewers

- `gh` is shelled out via `exec.Command` rather than pulled in as a Go
  dep. All calls go through a `bootstrapRunner` interface so tests
  don't hit the network.
- Unit tests use mocked runners; two real-git regression tests
  (`TestBootstrap_FreshMachine_*`) run real `git init`/`git commit`
  against a temp dir isolated via `HOME` + `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to
  prove the identity + gpgsign fixes end-to-end.
```
